newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian court adjourns Megawati case.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian court adjourns Megawati case.

text.p: A lawsuit filed by ousted Indonesian Democratc Party (PDI) chief Megawati Sukarnoputri against the government was adjourned for three weeks on Thursday after a brief hearing.

The case was held amid tight security as hundreds of troops and riot police surrounded the Central Jakarta State Court. Some 100 supporters of Megawati gathered outside but the morning passed off peacefully.
Lawyers for Megawati, the daughter of late founding president Sukarno, asked for an injunction to prevent a rival government-backed PDI faction from occupying party headquarters.
"We have asked for the status quo to be kept while the court case is in progress," Bambang Widjojanto, one of Megawati's lawyers, told Reuters after the hearing.
"The status quo means that Megawati remains as leader of the PDI and the PDI headquarters can be occupied (only by her). We want this decision or an injunction to be made first," he said.

The injunction would stop party rival Surjadi and his supporters from occupying the party headquarters, which was seized by police after a raid on July 27 to expel Megawati loyalists who had taken over the building.
After hearing the plaintiff's case, chief judge I Gde Ketut Sukarata adjourned the hearing until September 26 without making a decision.

Megawati is suing Interior Minister Yogie Memet, armed forces chief General Fiesal Tanjung, chief of police Lieutenant-General Dibyo Widodo and rival party leader Surjadi and his supporters for her ouster from the PDI leadership at a government-funded congress in June.

Her ouster led to anti-government protests unparalleled since President Suharto came to power three decades ago. The police raid on the PDI headquarters sparked riots in which at least five people were killed.
